page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-16 is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the c4n family. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) and 60.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring network-attached storage options for persistent data.

The instance does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a resource density perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable compute performance without resource sharing. The lack of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators like GPUs represents a design tradeoff, positioning this instance for workloads that rely on external storage systems and standard CPU-bound processing.

Given its balanced compute-to-memory ratio and dedicated vCPU allocation, the c4n-standard-16 is suited for general-purpose application hosting, web serving, containerized microservices, and moderate computational tasks. It is also applicable for CI/CD pipelines and distributed system nodes that do not require local high-speed disk access or GPU acceleration.
